Evidence/CLM-013
Evidence record

Financial-literacy activity does not establish capability outcomes

What does this evidence establish?

Global Money Week records of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) document financial-literacy activities during 2023–2025. Separately, the OECD/INFE 2023 adult financial-literacy survey, which covered 1,000 respondents in Yemen between 11 March and 1 April 2023, reports a financial well-being score of 15 out of 100 for Yemen and an overall financial-literacy score of 42 out of 100. These are different evidence classes: evidence that activities took place does not establish population capability or programme effectiveness.

What does it measure?

Two separate measures: the OECD/INFE 2023 financial-literacy and financial well-being scores (out of 100) for the Yemen sample, and records of Global Money Week financial-literacy activities from March 2023 to March 2025.

Who or what does it apply to?

Two separate evidence universes: the Yemen sample in the OECD/INFE 2023 adult financial-literacy survey, and source-stated Global Money Week audiences and participating bodies; not one combined population.

When was it measured or observed?

OECD/INFE 2023 survey; CBY-Aden programme activity, March 2023 to March 2025

How current is it?

The capability scores are from the OECD/INFE 2023 survey; the programme-activity record currently extends through March 2025. Neither is a 2026 capability outcome.

What this evidence does not establish

The OECD/INFE scores of 15 out of 100 (financial well-being) and 42 out of 100 (financial literacy) are not results of Global Money Week activity. Programme effectiveness is not established: that would require an evaluation with a baseline and appropriate follow-up measurement, which the activity records do not provide.

Limits of the measure

The OECD/INFE international report does not by itself resolve Yemen-specific sampling or coverage questions, so it is not established that the Yemen sample covers all areas or represents the national adult population.

Method and verification detailDetail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Two kinds of evidence are kept separate: the OECD/INFE 2023 adult financial-literacy survey, which covered 1,000 respondents in Yemen between 11 March and 1 April 2023, and the official Global Money Week programme and event records of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) for 2023 to 2025.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when a newer comparable population measure of financial capability, a programme evaluation or a correction to the source evidence is published.

How can I verify it?

This record is drawn from the source(s) listed on this page. Open a source record to reach the original document, and check that the definition, period, population and geography match what is stated here.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference.
